title: Martial Stances
why: "When you choose the Martial Artist subclass, take the Martial Stances sheet to track which stances your character knows." That is an instruction about setting a sheet up, and it is carried out once.
note: TRUE ORPHAN, and of the same kind as `ranger-companion`: a sheet built before play. Nobody reads this while four people wait — by the time a stance matters, the sheet already exists. It shares the property the other eight were excused for.

title: Stances
why: "You choose two stances from Tier 1 when you first take the Martial Artist's subclass foundation card... Mark a new stance from your tier or below each time you gain a level."
note: TRUE ORPHAN, and the same shape as `multiclassing`: a choice taken at a level-up, away from the table. The paragraph that opens it does define what a stance IS, but a definition is what the search box answers, not what a GM reaches for mid-scene.

title: Focus
why: "ONCE PER REST during a moment of calm, you can clear your mind and refocus your martial instincts. Clear your Focus track, then roll a number of d6s equal to your Instinct and gain Focus equal to the highest result rolled."
note: The section names its own moment. A rest is the between-scenes beat, and this is the only place in the product that says how the track refills — the app shipped the stepper before it shipped this sentence, which is why the section is here at all.

title: Shifting into Stances
why: "You can SPEND A FOCUS to shift into a martial stance and gain its effects... You can't shift into or have more than one active stance at a time."
note: A spend and a choice, made on your own turn, with a restriction that is checked at the moment of making it. `beastform-options` is the nearest neighbour already in the table and it holds `my-turn` for the same reason.

title: Dropping out of Stances
why: "You also drop out of your active stance when you TAKE SEVERE DAMAGE or MARK YOUR LAST HIT POINT."
note: ARGUED, not obvious, and the argument is worth recording because the section names two triggers and they fall in different moments. The one that surprises a table is the damage one: a Martial Artist who has just taken Severe damage has silently lost the stance they were counting on, and that is the sentence somebody needs read aloud. The other trigger — "at the end of the scene" — is housekeeping nobody has to be told. So this takes `damage` alone rather than `damage` and `between-scenes`, on the rule the ballot of 26 August used throughout: a moment is where the section is NEEDED, not everywhere it is true.
